text:
Parker Wotherspoon came to Vegas after a season in Pittsburgh, played in early October, then missed a month before the Golden Knights activated him on Nov. 11. He has been playing 18 minutes a night since, on a team that has won one of the five games he's played since coming back.

He doesn't score and isn't asked to. One assist in 11 games, no goals, 10 shots: that's the profile of a defense-first defenseman who shoots rarely and from the point. The Golden Knights do well with him on the ice, taking 59% of the expected goals at five on five, almost seven points better than without him, and they've scored 4.8 fewer goals than those chances deserve.

That makes him a quiet plus whose box score won't show it. Evolving-Hockey had him 72nd among defensemen last season, a solid middle-pair number. The Athletic's Jesse Granger questioned why he was "swinging his stick" at Thomas Harley's tying goal on Nov. 19, a reminder that one play is what people remember. Watch the shot share, not the points.
headline: Wotherspoon back on the Vegas blue line
